jurisdiction.name: Iraq
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Iraq has no AI law yet; AI governance is led from the Prime Minister's Office, whose adviser for scientific, academic and AI affairs drafts national policy under a Supreme Committee for AI chaired by the Prime Minister. In 2025 that office published a first-draft National AI Policy and a National Charter for AI Ethics, which proposes risk tiers, an AI ethics council and labelling of AI-generated content; neither has been formally adopted and the full national AI strategy was still being refined with the Ministry of Planning in 2026. Binding AI rules come so far from sector regulators: the Communications and Media Commission's Framework Regulations for Digital Platforms (in force 17 February 2025) require AI platforms to be licensed or notified, and the Central Bank of Iraq's 2025-2026 banking standards require deepfake and synthetic-identity safeguards. The CMC is now consulting on a dedicated AI Services Regulation (from 23 September 2026) with licensing, risk classification and outright bans on practices such as social scoring and mass biometric surveillance, alongside a digital-content draft that bans deceptive AI-generated content. Iraq has no general personal data protection law, which leaves AI data governance to sector rules and the drafts.
lead_institutions: Prime Minister's Office (Adviser for Scientific and Academic Affairs and AI; National AI Centre)
Supreme Committee for Artificial Intelligence (chaired by the Prime Minister)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 7 October 2026. The draft national AI policy and the AI ethics charter were read on the Prime Minister's Office AI portal, and the Communications and Media Commission's draft AI services regulation (in consultation until about 23 October 2026) was read from the published scan (key provisions; the middle articles are still to be read in detail). The websites of the Prime Minister's Office, the Ministry of Communications, Parliament and the Kurdistan Regional Government could not be read, so the Kurdistan Region pass is incomplete. The official gazette had no AI-specific instrument. A higher-education circular on AI tools in research is pending until an official copy is found.

instruments.current_status: Cover marked 'first draft 2025' (المسودة الأولى). Posted on the Prime Minister's Office AI portal (arabic.ai.gov.iq); the file was uploaded on 17 November 2025 per the portal's media record. No cabinet adoption found as of 2026-10-07; the full national AI strategy it is meant to lead into was still being refined with the Ministry of Planning in April 2026.
instruments.summary: First draft of Iraq's national AI policy, prepared by the committee drafting the national AI strategy under the Prime Minister (chair of the Supreme Committee for AI) with ministries, the CMC, UNESCO and ESCWA. It sets a vision of Iraq as a regional AI hub, applies to public and private sectors, and organises action under six axes (skills and jobs, R&D and entrepreneurship, data and infrastructure, priority sectors, international cooperation, enabling environment incl. AI legislation and an ethics charter). Governance would sit with the Supreme Council/Committee for AI, a new National AI Centre and an advisory committee, with annual review and monitoring indicators.

instruments.issuing_authority: Prime Minister's Office (Committee for Drafting the National AI Strategy)
instruments.publisher_name: Prime Minister's Office (Office of the Prime Minister's Adviser for Scientific and Academic Affairs and Artificial Intelligence)
instruments.current_status: Published on the Prime Minister's Office AI portal (file uploaded 17 November 2025 per the portal's media record). The document carries no adoption decision or date; it is not marked as a draft. Its prohibitions and the proposed national AI ethics council have no stated legal basis yet, so it is recorded as non-binding guidance.
instruments.summary: Ethics charter in 22 articles prepared under the Prime Minister's Office, applying to all public, private and non-profit bodies and individuals that develop or use AI. It sets core values (dignity, fairness, digital sovereignty, sustainability, reliability) and principles on non-discrimination and bias testing, privacy by design, explainability and disclosure of AI interaction, human oversight and complaints, safety, and green AI. It proposes an independent national AI ethics council, a three-tier risk classification (low / medium-high needing impact assessment and prior approval / prohibited, e.g. social scoring and lethal autonomous weapons), duties on generative-AI developers to curb deepfakes and watermark AI-generated content, and data localisation for sensitive national data.
metadata_gaps: Exact publication date (only the portal upload date is known)

instruments.english_title: Framework Regulations for Digital Platforms and Services
instruments.current_status: States it comes into force on 17 February 2025. Arabic and English versions published on cmc.iq (uploaded March 2025). The dedicated AI regulation it announces was put to consultation in September 2026.
instruments.summary: CMC framework regulation, issued under CPA Order No. 65 of 2004, that brings digital platforms serving users in Iraq under licensing, registration or notification. 'Artificial-intelligence platforms' are an in-scope category: locally based AI platforms need a CMC licence and foreign-based ones must notify. AI platforms share the user-generated-content duties (moderation, transparency of content policies, automated plus human review, appeals), and Article 6.1.5 requires compliance with Iraqi AI rules and announces a forthcoming CMC AI regulation.
metadata_gaps: Exact issue date (only the 17 February 2025 effective date is stated)

instruments.english_title: Draft Regulation on Artificial Intelligence Services in the Republic of Iraq (public consultation)
instruments.current_status: Opened for public consultation on 23 September 2026 for 30 days (comments to enquiries@cmc.iq), so open until about 23 October 2026. The PDF is a scanned 25-page document watermarked 'draft prepared for review and approval after public consultation' (Annex 4); text was read from page images.
instruments.summary: Draft CMC regulation (Annex 4 to the 2025 digital-platforms framework) that would license all entities offering AI-based services in Iraq, including foreign services aimed at Iraqi users, on separate software and hardware tracks with risk classes. It bans outright mass biometric surveillance in public spaces without a court order, social scoring, AI built to manipulate opinion or spread disinformation, harmful AI aimed at children, autonomous lethal weapons and AI that breaks Iraqi law, and sets ethics, risk-assessment, generative/general-purpose AI, data-governance and digital-sovereignty, consumer-complaint, inspection and penalty provisions. Government applications are exempt from fees and licensing but must meet its cybersecurity and data-protection rules.
metadata_gaps: Scanned PDF without a text layer; article-level detail read from page images

instruments.english_title: Draft Regulation on Digital Content in Iraq (public consultation)
instruments.current_status: Put to public consultation by the CMC on 13 September 2026; no closing date stated in the announcement. Not adopted as of 2026-10-07.
instruments.summary: Draft CMC regulation on digital content available to or aimed at the public in Iraq, issued under Order No. 65 of 2004 and integrated with the 2025 digital-platforms framework. Article 28 (disinformation, forgery and digital manipulation) prohibits misleading fake content, expressly including the use of AI or digital processing to produce content that deceives the public as to its authenticity. It also sets duties for platforms and digital service providers on reporting mechanisms, takedown, blocking and compliance.

instruments.english_title: CBI Detailed Assessment Guide for the 2026 Standards – Digital Banks
instruments.current_status: Listed on the CBI banking-supervision page under 14 April 2026 with the digital-bank licensing rules, standards handbook and timeline. The guide states that the circular takes effect from its publication date and applies exclusively to all digital banks.
instruments.summary: Mandatory CBI guide detailing how the 2026 standards for the new digital-bank licence class are assessed (ownership and governance, core banking, online banking, risk and compliance). For digital onboarding it requires safeguards against identity fraud through technologies that detect and prevent deepfakes and synthetic identities generated by AI, alongside liveness checks. The AI-specific content is limited to this anti-fraud requirement.

instruments.english_title: CBI Detailed Assessment Guide for the 2025 Standards – Private Commercial and Islamic Banks (Banking Reform 2025)
instruments.current_status: Part of the CBI Banking Reform 2025 package listed on the CBI banking-reform project page; the guide states the reform enters into force in August 2025 and that its requirements are mandatory. No exact issue date is shown on the listing.
instruments.summary: Mandatory CBI guide setting out how the 2025 banking-reform standards are assessed for private commercial and Islamic banks, read with the standards handbook and the reform-paths circular. Its electronic-onboarding requirements oblige banks to deploy technologies that detect and prevent deepfakes and AI-generated synthetic identities. Other content covers governance, ownership, risk management and technology systems and is not AI-specific.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched, nothing found to record for: public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, international, historical. Iraq has no general personal data protection law or data-protection authority (the CMC's 2025 framework says a PDP law will follow); no AI-specific public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, standards (COSQC), sandbox or index instruments were found; no national AI treaty ratification (UNESCO Recommendation is handled at regional level). Kurdistan Region: no AI instrument found, but gov.krd blocks automated reading. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. Previous file had no instruments; 7 added, none removed. The AI policy draft and ethics charter come from the PM Office AI portal (arabic.ai.gov.iq, linked from ai.gov.iq); both PDFs were read in full. The CMC AI services draft is a scanned PDF without a text layer: title, contents, preamble, scope, exemptions and prohibited uses were read from page images. CMC upload paths use a decomposed hamza (ي + U+0654) in file names; the URLs stored here are the working percent-encoded forms. Blocked to automated reading: pmo.iq (403), moc.gov.iq (403), iq.parliament.iq (403), gov.krd and dit.gov.krd (403), gds.gov.iq (proxy 502); cabinet.iq serves only a script shell. Al-Waqa'i al-Iraqiya (moj.gov.iq) search found no AI-specific gazette instrument. The National Development Plan 2024-2028 mentions AI only in passing (no AI pillar), so it is not recorded. A MOHESR circular of 3 March 2026 on AI tools in research is held as a lead: the only copy is on a university site, and the guide itself is behind a QR link that no longer resolves. Subnational pass (Kurdistan Region): no KRG AI instrument found, but the KRG portal could not be read. Sweep: no adoption of the national AI policy, ethics charter or national AI strategy found by 2026-10-07; the CMC AI draft consultation runs to about 23 October 2026.
